articles.title: How to Play the Silent Hill Games in Order
articles.summary: Silent Hill has appeared in the restless dreams of horror fans for almost three decades now. The foggy town and its various iterations, plagued by the Otherworld, continue to define the mechanics and ambience of psychological horror to this day.
body: Each Silent Hill game contains a relatively standalone story, tied to whatever character the Otherworld has decided to bring to its doorstep. However, the lore of Silent Hill develops across games through returning characters as well as memos, posters, and other small details. Despite its fill of contradictions, some of which are only natural for games with multiple endings, there’s a larger story lurking in the background of each protagonist’s path to atonement (or madness).
If the release of Silent Hill: Townfall has sparked your curiosity about how the timeline all fits together, we’ve got you covered.
Approximately 18 Silent Hill games have been released since the franchise debuted in 1999.

Four Silent Hill games were originally developed by Team Silent between 1999 and 2004. Subsequent games, including plenty of spinoffs, were developed by a variety of studios across Japan and North America.

articles.title: Microsoft CEO Attempts To Kill Remaining Xbox Goodwill
articles.summary: After Xbox laid off 1,600 employees over the summer, Microsoft's gaming division followed up with more layoffs and studio closures this week. In the wake of these events, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is taking a look at the bright side and praising Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's actions as a necessary step.
body: "There's some amount of streamlining the team is doing, and Asha is doing, which is great to see," said Nadella during his appearance on the Sources Podcast. He also noted that he feels "fantastic about the IP we have right now. If I look at the studios, the IP portfolio we have, and our ability to then take that and produce great games going forward, I feel fantastic."
"We have to invent the right sustainable business model that allows us to deliver gaming to more and more people," added Nadella.
Regarding AI, Nadella questioned why Western consumers are so skeptical about the technology compared to other parts of the world.

Prominent AI skeptic Ed Zitron has blamed Xbox's precarious position on " catastrophic mismanagement " by Microsoft and AI bets that didn't pan out. Even after the most recent layoffs, there are indications that more job cuts are coming to Xbox.
points: After Xbox laid off 1,600 employees over the summer, Microsoft's gaming division followed up with more layoffs and studio closures this week.

articles.title: Infinity Festival Returns to Los Angeles in November With a Focus on AI
articles.summary: Infinity Festival, an annual event celebrating the convergence of entertainment, technology, and creativity, is returning to Los Angeles this November for its 9th edition.
body: In previous years, the festival has hosted guests like Avengers directors the Russo Brothers, Brie Larson, Jon Favreau, Project Hail Mary directors Phil Lord and Chris Miller, Jeff Bridges, and many more. This year, the festival promises to dive deep into AI, with panels focusing on its “growing role across the creative industries.” Instead of a standalone track, AI will be present through a broader program “spanning animation, gaming, sports tech, filmmaking, music, virtual production, and live entertainment.”

At the event, AI-focused programming will “explore the evolving tools and workflows behind animation and filmmaking, the growing crossover between gaming and entertainment, new technologies reshaping live sports and fan experiences, as well as advances in immersive production and live event design.”

Additionally, longtime partners like NVIDIA and HP will participate in the festival’s 2026 programming slate, which will feature “panels, keynotes, screenings, demonstrations, and exhibitions, with speakers and programming to be announced in the coming weeks.”

articles.title: Viral Resident Evil Stunt Footage Shows the Wild Way the 'Katamari Monster' Came to Life in Zach Cregger's Movie
articles.summary: With Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie now in theaters, staff who worked on the film are sharing behind-the-scenes footage of how it all came together, including a jaw-dropping look at the stunt team behind one of its monsters. Warning: Spoilers for Resident Evil ahead!
body: Resident Evil is known for its wide variety of zombies, but some of the mutations we saw in Cregger’s version of events were brand-new and extremely gnarly. The main stalker monster of the film has been a hot topic of discussion within the games’ fanbase, with many affectionately dubbing it the ‘Katamari Monster.’

If you’ve seen the film and played the Katamari games, you’ll immediately understand why it’s been given this humorous moniker; its specific mutation includes some tentacle-like creatures that reach for other infected bodies and combine them into a mass of arms and legs that rolls around town, much like a Katamari.

Most viewers, myself included, figured this monster was a pure work of CGI. But astonishingly, this isn’t the case, as one of the stunt performers tasked with creating its movements proved in a now-viral Instagram post.

Jakub Hudlicky, a performer with Movement Production in the Czech Republic, published a series of videos showing himself and several other stuntpeople all strapped together with vests. Working together, the team made their way from one side of a soundstage to another, just like how the Katamari monster moved in Cregger’s film.

articles.title: This Diablo 4 Trick Lets You Become Stronger Than Ever, But It Might Not Be Intended
articles.summary: Diablo 4 players are decking themselves out in full sets of Mythic Unique gear as part of Season 15, resulting in characters that are more powerful than ever before. Whether that was Blizzard's goal, or this is simply a mistake of some kind, is currently up for debate.
body: It's about as big of a change from one season to the next that Diablo 4 has ever experienced. Back in Season 14, Blizzard added the "crafted" item tag to Mythic Uniques made via the Horadric Cube, Blacksmith, or Jeweler, with a limit of only one crafted Mythic being equippable at a time. Even if you had the Resplendent Sparks resource needed to make more Mythics, you couldn't use them. Instead, you had to rely on good old-fashioned luck to find natural Mythic drops without the crafted tag.

The changes weren't popular, so Blizzard walked it back mid-season, and has made further improvements as part of the latest season, Hell's Legacy. Mythics made by the Blacksmith or Jeweler are no longer considered "crafted," while ones made via the cube still are. Once again, players could have several Mythics of your own creation equipped at once, much like the previous seasons.
However, for players with more sparks than they know what to do with, there is technically a way to get around the "crafted" tag.

articles.title: 10 Free Browser Games That are Actually Fun to Play
articles.summary: If you do your research, though, you’ll find a treasure trove of easily-accessible gems — like a solo dev’s reworked Diablo village where you watch your party auto-battle its way through catacombs, or an idle game where managing catnip supply chains spirals into deep-space civilization management.
body: All of these games cost the exact same amount: Nothing. Pull one up in your browser right now — no sunk cost, no download, no account to make. Bookmark whichever ones pull you in. You won’t pay anything, but you might lose countless hours to catnip management or paperclip production on these free browser games. Don’t say we didn’t warn you.
Play this if: You like Slay the Spire, but wish the cards were dice instead.

Die in the Dungeon Classic swaps your familiar rogue deckbuilder game’s cards for dice. In this game, you play a frog warrior descending through a dungeon, placing attack (red), defense (blue), heal (green), and boost (purple) dice onto a diamond-shaped grid each turn. Some dice stick around for multiple turns. Others shatter after a single use. Will you think ahead or go with a flashier instant-gratification strategy? What’s not a roll of the dice is this game’s impression — it’s currently sitting at a 4.7-star rating across nearly 3,000 ratings on itch.io.

articles.title: Yes, Beyond Good & Evil 2 Is Somehow Still In Development
articles.summary: No news is good news, they say. They also say that some news, however little, is good news, too, and girl, do we have some news: Ubisoft's struggling action-adventure game Beyond Good & Evil 2 is still alive despite remaining in development hell.
body: Ubisoft Bordeaux's lead writer and associate narrative director Rik Godwin took to Bluesky on September 22 to provide a brief update on the game.

"Odd sort of non-announcement but for the past few months I've been working on Beyond Good & Evil 2 in a support/consultant role," Godwin, who was a writer on Assassin's Creed Shadows, said. "I am allowed to say this, I checked."

It makes sense that Ubisoft Bordeaux would assist with Beyond Good & Evil 2. According to IGN, Ubisoft Montpellier, which is leading the project's development, is just south of the Bordeaux studio. And although Ubisoft Bordeaux was the lead developer on both 2023's Assassin's Creed Mirage and Shadows' 2025 expansion Claws of Awaji, that studio typically operates in a support role for Ubisoft's myriad other teams.

articles.title: Alan Ritchson's 2019 Sports Comedy is Free to Watch on YouTube
articles.summary: Sports movies have a pretty impressive track record when it comes to becoming classics. From Rocky and Field of Dreams to Remember the Titans and Moneyball, there are plenty of movies that have managed to stick around in the cultural conversation long after they first hit theaters.
body: But not every sports movie has to be a big-budget classic. Sometimes you just want something silly, easy to watch, and fun enough to kill a couple of hours. And if that's what you're after, one of the goofiest sports movies is now free to watch on YouTube.

The Turkey Bowl, a 2019 sports comedy starring Alan Ritchson, is currently available to watch for free on YouTube. You can watch it right now without a subscription, though you'll have to sit through a few ads along the way.

The Turkey Bowl centers on a group of friends who return home for Thanksgiving and revive an annual tradition: a flag football game that has been going on for years. What should be a casual holiday get-together quickly becomes much more serious when old rivalries resurface, with the players determined to finally settle the score on the football field.

As the game gets increasingly competitive, the movie leans into the chaos of a bunch of adults treating a backyard Thanksgiving football game like the Super Bowl. Alongside Ritchson, the cast includes Matt Jones ( Breaking Bad ), Ryan Hansen ( Veronica Mars ), Leah McKendrick ( The Movie Critic ), and Jacob Wysocki ( Pitch Perfect ).

articles.title: Switch Pirate Ignored Nintendo’s Lawsuit, Now He Owes $4.5 Million
articles.summary: After suing a former Reddit moderator in October 2025 for pirating Switch games, a Washington court has ordered the individual in question to pay Nintendo $4.5 million in damages.
body: According to a September 25 TorrentFreak report, US District Judge Lauren King ordered former r/SwitchPirates moderator James "Archbox" Williams to cough up $4.5 million in damages to Nintendo after the company accused him of operating several pirate shops to illegally decrypt and distribute Switch games to the public.

The lawsuit, which was filed in a Washington federal court in June 2024, stated that Williams had been running this racket since at least 2019, using "circumvention device" software to bypass the company's systems and gain access to over 30 Nintendo Switch games. This includes titles like The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, and Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.

Williams reportedly ignored the complaint at the time, which prompted Nintendo to seek the statutory maximum of $150,000 per title in October 2025. And just this week, Judge King agreed with Nintendo's request, stating that Williams was aware of the case, as he both hired a lawyer to object to a Google subpoena and continued posting on Reddit but opted to not respond to the company's lawsuit.
points: After suing a former Reddit moderator in October 2025 for pirating Switch games, a Washington court has ordered the individual in question to pay Nintendo $4.5 million in damages.

articles.title: Skyrim loremaster says The Elder Scrolls never got a Fallout: New Vegas-style game because Bethesda is "very protective" over its golden goose
articles.summary: Skyrim launched almost 15 years ago while The Elder Scrolls 6 is still marinating over at Bethesda Game Studios. body: That's according to Kurt Kuhlmann, a lead Skyrim developer and the fantasy series' former loremaster, who told the FRVR podcast that Bethesda is apparently too protective over its golden goose to let anyone else tackle a mainline-style game.
Bethesda supposedly didn't want those sentiments to follow The Elder Scrolls, as well - Kuhlmann said he doesn't think director Todd Howard "wanted to create that situation again."

"Todd, from my time there, he is very protective of it," Kuhlmann added. "I do think [The Elder Scrolls Online] took the heat off… there was a new Elder Scrolls product and it was ongoing. It was creating new content constantly. There are a lot of people, I mean, I know the single-player people, I'm one of those people–but there are a lot of people to whom The Elder Scrolls is now ESO. That’s their experience with it. That's what they love. That's where they got their Elder Scrolls gaming experience, and that's probably what they want more of."

articles.title: I did the math on my Wardogs XP grind, and now I wish I hadn't
articles.summary: I've had this goal in the back of my head to unlock all the Medic gear in Wardogs so I can become the best sawbones on the server. There's only one piece I still don't have—a medical bag that can both revive and heal teammates in one item.
body: But this week I noticed my steady Medic rise had slowed considerably. I had been ranking up every one or two rounds, but now I'm lucky to climb a rank over a whole night of play. I'm doing just as well in matches—better than ever, actually, with the addition of defibrillators and stronger medkits—so that's not the issue.

For the first time, I made note of the XP thresholds for leveling up and compared where I'm at to my goal. I wish I hadn't. So far I've gained 17 levels with 177,619 Medic XP. Level 24, just seven ranks later, will require 337,000 XP. So while it looks like I'm gaining on that useful medicine bag, I'm actually just 52% of the way there.
So this is the brutal Wardogs grind I've been hearing about. Bummer.

I was curious how that last 48% will translate to playtime and matches—maybe it'll go by faster than it sounds—so I did an unscientific test: I played an average match with my typical focus on revives and healing. For the record: I'm an OK player at best. To maximise XP gains, I also brought an SMG and purchased stims to administer to teammates.
points: I've had this goal in the back of my head to unlock all the Medic gear in Wardogs so I can become the best sawbones on the server.

videos.summary: Pre-order and play the free demo for FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE now on Nintendo Switch 2:
body: Take a first look at content and features included in the first HD 2D FINAL FANTASY!

The pixel-art world of FINAL FANTASY returns in this reimagined adventure! The world is full of secrets, including the wandering swordmaster Gilgamesh, a Colosseum with deadly monsters and rewards to match, the Chamber of Arms with formidable foes sealed within legendary weapons, and a showdown with Ultima Weapon. Try out the first chapter in the free demo!
